transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: No.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: There are many people who believe that the only way we can get this country turned around is to tax the middle class more and punish them more, but the truth is that middle-class Americans are basically the only group of Americans who’ve been taxed more in the 1980s and during the last 12 years, even though their incomes have gone down.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The wealthiest Americans have been taxed much less, even though their incomes have gone up.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Middle-class people will have their fair share of changing to do, and many challenges to face, including the challenge of becoming constantly re-educated.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But my plan is a departure from trickle-down economics, just cutting taxes on the wealthiest Americans and getting out of the way.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It’s also a departure from tax-and- spend economics, because you can’t tax and divide an economy that isn’t growing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I propose an American version of what works in other countries — I think we can do it better: invest and grow.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I believe we can increase investment and reduce the deficit at the same time, if we not only ask the wealthiest Americans and foreign corporations to pay their share; we also provide over $100 billion in tax relief, in terms of incentives for new plants, new small businesses, new technologies, new housing, and for middle class families; and we have $140 billion of spending cuts.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Invest and grow.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Raise some more money, spend the money on tax incentives to have growth in the private sector, take the money from the defense cuts and reinvest it in new transportation and communications and environmental clean-up systems.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: This will work.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: On this, as on so many other issues, I have a fundamental difference from the present administration.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I don’t believe trickle down economics will work.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Unemployment is up.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Most people are working harder for less money than they were making 10 years ago.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think we can do better if we have the courage to change.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Do I have 1 minute?

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Just the ground rules here.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, he doesn’t like trickle down government but I think he’s talking about the Reagan-Bush years where we created 15 million jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The rich are paying a bigger percent of the total tax burden.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And what I don’t like is trickle down government.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And therein, I think Governor Clinton keeps talking about trickle down, trickle down, and he’s still talking about spending more and taxing more.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Government — he says invest government, grow government.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Government doesn’t create jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: If they do, they’re make-work jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s the private sector that creates jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And yes, we’ve got too many taxes on the American people and we’re spending too much.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And that’s why I want to get the deficit down by controlling the growth of mandatory spending.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It won’t be painless.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Perot put his finger on something there.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It won’t be painless but we’ve got to get the job done.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But not by raising taxes.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: and Mrs.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: America, when you hear him say we’re going to tax only the rich, watch your wallet because his figures don’t add up and he’s going to sock it right to the middle class taxpayer and lower, if he’s going to pay for all the spending programs he proposes.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So we have a big difference on this trickle down theory.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I do not want any more trickle down government.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s gotten too big.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want to do something about that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: The basic problem with it, it doesn’t balance the budget.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: If you forecast it out, we still have a significant deficit under each of their plans, as I understand them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Our challenge is to stop the financial bleeding.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: If you take a patient into the hospital that’s bleeding arterially, step one is to stop the bleeding.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And we are bleeding arterially.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: There’s only one way out of this, and that is to stop the deterioration of our job base, to have a growing, expanding job base, to give us the tax base — see, balancing the budget is not nearly as difficult as paying off the $4 trillion debt and leaving our children the American dream intact.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We have spent their money.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to pay it back.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: This is going to take fair, shared sacrifice.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: My plan balances the budget within 6 years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We didn’t do it faster than that because we didn’t want to disrupt the economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We gave it off to a slow start and a fast finish to give the economy time to recover.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: But we faced it and we did it, and we believe it’s fair, shared sacrifice.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: The one thing I have done is lay it squarely on the table in front of the American people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: You’ve had a number of occasions to see in detail what the plan is, and at least you’ll understand it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I think that’s fundamental in our country, that you know what you’re getting into.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I disagree with both of them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: For one thing, let me just follow up here.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I disagree with Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Perot that the answer is to raise — put a 50-cent gas tax on the middle class and raise more taxes on the middle class and the working poor than on the wealthy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: His own analysis says that unemployment will be slightly higher in 1995 under his plan than it is today.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And as far as what Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Bush says, he is the person who raised taxes on the middle class after saying he wouldn’t.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And just this year, Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Bush vetoed a tax increase on the wealthy that gave middle class tax relief.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: He vetoed middle class tax relief this year.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And furthermore, under this administration, spending has increased more than it has in the last 20 years and he asked Congress to spend more money than it actually spent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Now, it’s hard to out-spend Congress but he tried to for the last 3 years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So my view is the middle class is the — they’ve been suffering, Jim.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Now, should people pay more for Medicare if they can?

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Yes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Should they pay more for Social Security if they get more out of it than they paid in, they’re upper income people?

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Yes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But look what’s happened to the middle class.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Middle class Americans are working harder for less money than they were making ten years ago and they’re paying higher taxes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The tax burden on them has not gone down.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It has gone up.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think the answer is to slow the economy down more, drive unemployment up more and undermine the health of the private sector.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The answer is to invest and grow this economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That’s what works in other countries and that’s what’ll work here.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think everybody’s paying too much taxes.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He refers to one tax increase.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Let me remind you it was a Democratic tax increase, and I didn’t want to do it and I went along with it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I said I make a mistake.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: If I make a mistake, I admit it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s quite different than some.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But I think that’s the American way.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think everyone’s paying too much, but I think this idea that you can go out and — then he hits me for vetoing a tax bill.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Yes, I did.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And the American taxpayer ought to be glad they have a president to stand up to a spending Congress.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We remember what it was like when we had a spending president and a spending Congress, and interest rates — who remembers that?

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: They were at 21.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: 5% under Jimmy Carter, and inflation was 15.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We don’t want to go back to that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And so yes, everybody’s taxed too much and I want to get the taxes down, but not by signing a tax bill that’s gonna raise taxes on people.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, the record in Arkansas.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I mean, look at it, and that’s what we’re asking America to have?

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Now look, he says Arkansas’s a poor state.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: They are.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But in almost every category they’re lagging.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’ll give you an example.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He talks about all the jobs he’s created in one or 2 years.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Over the last ten years since he’s been governor, they’re 30% behind, 30% — they’re 30% of the national average.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: On pay for teachers, on all these categories, Arkansas is right near the very bottom.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You haven’t heard me mention this before, but we’re getting close now and I think it’s about time I start putting things in perspective.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I’m going to do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s not dirty campaigning because he’s been talking about my record for a half a year here, 11 months here.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So we’ve got to do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I gotta get it in perspective.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: What’s his mistake?

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Admit it, that Arkansas is doing very, very badly against any standard — environment, support for police officers, whatever it is.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Bush’s Bureau of Labor Statistics says that Arkansas ranks first in the country in the growth of new jobs this year, first.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: This year.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: 4th in manufacturing jobs, 4th in the reduction of poverty, 4th in income increase.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Over the last 10 years we’ve created manufacturing jobs much more rapidly than the national average.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Over the last 5 years our income has grown more rapidly than the national average.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We are 2nd in tax burden, the 2nd lowest tax burden in the country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We have the lowest per capita state and local spending in the country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We’re low spending, low tax burden.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We dramatically increased investment and our jobs are growing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I wish America had that kind of record and I think most people looking at us tonight would like it if we had more jobs and a lower spending burden on the government.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I grew up 5 blocks from Arkansas.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Let’s put it in perspective.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: It’s a beautiful state.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: It’s a fairly rural state.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: It has a population less than Chicago or Los Angeles, about the size of Dallas and Forth Worth combined.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: So I think probably we’re making a mistake night after night after night to cast the nation’s future on a unit that small.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: It’s irrelevant.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: No, no, no, but I could say, you know, that I ran a small grocery store on the corner, therefore I extrapolate that into the fact that I can run Wal-Mart.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: That’s not true.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I can’t protect an Arkansas company, you notice there, Governor.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Perot, with all respect, I think it is highly relevant, and I think that a 4-billion dollar budget of state and federal funds is not all that small, and I think the fact that I took a state that was one of the poorest states in the country and had been for 153 years and tried my best to modernize its economy and to make the kind of changes that have generated support from people like the presidents of Apple Computer and Hewlett-Packard and some of the biggest companies in this country, 24 retired generals and admirals and hundreds of business executives, are highly relevant.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And, you know, I’m frankly amazed that since you grew up 5 blocks from there you would think that what goes on in that state is irrelevant.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think it’s been pretty impressive.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: It’s not —

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And the people who have jobs — The people who have jobs and educations and opportunities that didn’t have them 10 years ago don’t think it’s irrelevant at all; they think it’s highly relevant and they wish the rest of the country had them.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t have a dog in this fight, but I’d like to get in on this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Well, you think it’s relevant.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Governor Clinton has to operate under a balanced budget amendment — he has to do it, that is the law.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’d like to see a balanced budget amendment for America, to protect the American taxpayers, and then that would discipline not only the executive branch but the spending Congress, the Congress that’s been in control of one party, his party, for 38 years.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And we almost had it done.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And that institution, the House of Representatives — everyone is yelling “Clean House!

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: ” One of the reasons is we almost had it done, and the speaker — a very, able, decent fellow, I might add — but he twisted the arms of some of the sponsors of that legislation and had them change their vote.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: What’s relevant here is that tool, that discipline, that he has to live by in Arkansas, and I’d like it for the American people.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want the line-item veto.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want a check-off, so if the Congress can’t do it, let people check off their income tax, 10% of it, to compel the government to cut spending.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And if they can’t do it, if the Congress can’t do it, let them then have to do it across the board.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s what we call a sequester.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s the discipline we need, and I’m working for that — to protect the American taxpayer against the big spenders.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Jim, I don’t think that’s a fair shot.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I hear it — I hear it echoed by political opponents.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But I don’t think it’s fair.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think we’ve been fighting from day one to do something about the inner cities.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m for enterprise zones.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I have had it in every single proposal I’ve sent to the Congress.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And now we hear a lot of talk, oh, well, we all want enterprise zones, and yet the House and the Senate can’t send it down without loading it up with a lot of, you know, these Christmas tree ornaments they put on the legislation.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think in racial harmony that I’m a laggard on that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’ve been speaking out since day 1.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’ve gotten the Americans for Disabilities Act, which I think is one of the foremost pieces of civil rights legislation.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And yes, it took me to veto 2 civil rights quota bills because I don’t believe in quotas, and I don’t think the American people believe in quotas.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I beat back the Congress on that, and then we passed a decent civil rights bill that offers guarantees against discrimination in employment.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And that is good.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’ve spoken out over and over again against antisemitism and racism, and I think my record as a member of Congress speaks for itself on that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: What was the other part of it?

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think that’s true at all.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think that’s true, but you know, let others fire away on it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I’d like to just talk about issues, and so —

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Well, no, but the point is that’s a subjective thing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: See, the subjective thing is when does President Bush react?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And it would be very difficult for me to answer that in any short period of time.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I thought you’d forgotten I was here.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I will let the American people decide that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I would rather not critique the 2 candidates.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The only thing I would say about that is, I think that on the economy, Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Bush said for a long time there was no recession, and then said it would be better to do nothing than to have a compromise effort with the Congress.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: He really didn’t have a new economic program until over 1300 days into his presidency, and not all of his health care initiative has been presented to the Congress even now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think it’s important to elect a president who is committed to getting this economy going again, and who realizes we have to abandon trickle-down economics and put the American people first again, and who will send programs to the Congress in the first hundred days to deal with the critical issues that America is crying out for leadership on — jobs, incomes, the health care crisis, the need to control the economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Those things deserve to be dealt with from day one.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I will deal with them from day 1.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: They will be my first priority, not my election year concern.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, I think you’re overlooking that we have had major accomplishments in the first term.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But if you’re talking about protecting the taxpayer against his friends in the US Congress, go back to what it was like when you had a Democratic president and a Democratic Congress.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You don’t have to go back to Herbert Hoover.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Go back to Jimmy Carter, and interest rates were 21%, inflation was 15%.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The misery index — unemployment and inflation added together — it was invented by the Democrats — went right through the roof.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’ve cut it in half.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And all you hear about is how bad things are.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You know, remember the question, are you better off?

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, is a homebuyer better off he can refinance the home, because interest rates are down?

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Is the senior citizen better off because inflation is not wiping out their family’s savings?

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think they are.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Is the guy out of work better off?

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Of course he’s not, but he’s not gonna be better off if we grow the government, if we invest, as Governor Clinton says, invest in more government.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You’ve got to free up the private sector.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You’ve got to let small businesses have more incentives.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: For 3 months — quarters I’ve been fighting, 3 quarters been fighting to get the Congress to pass some incentives for small business.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Capital gains, investment tax allowance, credit for first- time homebuyers.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And it’s blocked by the Congress.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And then if a little of it comes my way, they load it up with Christmas trees and tax increases, and I have to stand up and favor the taxpayer.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I think the General Motors thing is very relevant.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I did everything I could to get General Motors to face its problems in the mid-’80s while it was still financially strong.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: They just wouldn’t do it, and everybody now knows the terrible price they’re paying by waiting until it’s obvious to the brain-dead that they have problems.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now, hundreds, thousands of good, decent people, whole cities up here in this state are adversely impacted because they would not move in a timely way.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Our government is that point now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: The thing that I am in this race for is to tap the American people on the shoulder and to say to every single one of you, fix it while we’re still relatively strong.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: If you have a heart problem, you don’t wait till a heart attack to address it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: So the General Motors experience is relevant.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: At the point when I could not get them to address those problems, I had created so much stress in the board, who wanted to just keep the Lawrence Welk music going, that they asked to buy my remaining shares.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I sold them my remaining shares.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: They went their way.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I went my way because it was obvious we had a complete disagreement about what should be done with the company.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: But let’s take my life in perspective.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Again and again, on complex, difficult tasks, I have stayed the course.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: When I was asked by our government to do the POW project, within a year the Vietnamese had sent people into Canada to make arrangements to have me and my family killed.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And I had 5 small children, and my family and I decided we would stay the course, and we lived with that problem for 3 years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Then I got into the Texas War on Drugs program and the big-time drug dealers got all upset.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Then when I had 2 people imprisoned in Iran, I could have left them there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I could have rationalized it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We went over, we got them out, we brought them back home.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And since then, for years, I have lived with the burden of the Middle East, where it’s eye for an eye and tooth for a tooth country, in terms of their unhappiness with the fact that I was successful in that effort.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Again and again and again, in the middle of the night, at 2 or 3 o’clock in the morning, my government has called me to take extraordinary steps for Americans in distress, and again and again and again I have responded.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And I didn’t wilt and I didn’t quit.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now, what happened in July we’ve covered again and again and again.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: But I think in terms of the American people’s concern about my commitment, I’m here tonight, folks; I never quit supporting you as you put me on the ballot in the other 26 states; and when you asked me to come back in, I came back in.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And talk about not quitting, I’m spending my money on this campaign; the 2 parties are spending your money, taxpayer money.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I put my wallet on the table for you and your children.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Over $60 million at least will go into this campaign to leave the American dream to you and your children, to get this country straightened out, because if anybody owes it to you, I do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I’ve lived the American dream; I’d like for your children to be able to live it, too.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I don’t have any criticism of Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Perot.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think what I’d like to talk about a minute, since you’re asking the question, is the General Motors issue.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think there’s any question that the automobile executives made some errors in the 1980s, but I also think we should look at how much productivity has increased lately, how much labor has done to increase productivity and how much management has done.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And we’re still losing a lot of auto jobs, in my judgment, because we don’t have a national economic strategy that will build the industrial base of this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Just today I met with the presidents and the vice presidents of the Willow Run union here, near here.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: They both said they were Vietnam veterans supporting me because I had an economic program to put them back to work.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We need an investment incentive to modernize plant and equipment; we’ve got to control the health care costs for those people — otherwise we can’t keep the manufacturing jobs here; and we need a tough trade policy that is fair, that insists on open markets in return for open markets.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We ought to have a strategy that will build the economic and industrial base.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So I think Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Perot was right in questioning the management practices.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But they didn’t have much of a partner in government here as compared with the policies the Germans and the Japanese followed, and I believe we can do better.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That’s one of the things I want to change.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I know that we can grow manufacturing jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We did it in my state, and we can do it nationally.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: To this?

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, I wondered, when Governor Clinton was talking to the auto workers, whether he talked about his and Senator Gore’s favoring CAFE standards, fuel efficiency standards, of 40 miles per gallon.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That would break the auto industry and throw a lot of people out of work.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: As regarding Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Perot, I take back something I said about him.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I once said, in a frivolous moment, when he got out of the race: If you can’t stand the heat, buy an air conditioning company.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I take it back, because I think — he said he made a mistake.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And the thing I find is if I make a mistake, I admit it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’ve never heard Governor Clinton make a mistake.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But one mistake he’s made is fuel efficiency standards at 40 to 45 miles a gallon will throw many auto workers out of work, and you can’t have it both ways.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: There’s a pattern here of appealing to the auto workers and then trying to appeal to the spotted owl crowds or the extremes in the environmental movement.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You can’t do it as president: you can’t have a pattern of one side of the issue one day and another the next.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So my argument is not with Ross Perot; it is more with Governor Clinton.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Let’s just talk about the CAFE standards — that’s the fuel efficiency standards.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: They are now 27.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: 5 miles per gallon per automobile fleet.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I never said — and I defy you to find where I said — I gave an extensive environmental speech in April, and I said that we ought to have a goal of raising the fuel efficiency standards to 40 miles a gallon.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think that should be a goal.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I have never said we should write it into law if there is evidence that that goal cannot be achieved.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The Natl Science Foundation did a study which said it would be difficult for us to reach fuel efficiency standards in excess of 37 miles per gallon by the year 2000.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think we should try to raise the fuel efficiency.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And let me say this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think we ought to have incentives to do it, I think we ought to push to do it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That doesn’t mean we have to write it into the law.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Look, I am a job creator, not a job destroyer.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It is the Bush administration that has had no new jobs in the private sector in the last 4 years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: In my state, we’re leading the country in private sector job growth.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But it is good for America to improve fuel efficiency.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We also ought to convert more vehicles to compressed natural gas.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That’s another way to improve the environment.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Well, everybody’s nibbling around the edges.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Let’s go to the center of the bull’s-eye, the core problem.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And believe me, everybody on the factory floor all over this country knows it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: You implement that NAFTA, the Mexican trade agreement, where they pay people a dollar an hour, have no health care, no retirement, no pollution controls, et cetera, et cetera, et cetera, and you’re going to hear a giant sucking sound of jobs being pulled out of this country right at a time when we need the tax base to pay the debt and pay down the interest on the debt and get our house back in order.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to proceed very carefully on that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: See, there’s a lot I don’t understand.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I do understand business.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I do understand creating jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I do understand how to make things work.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And I got a long history of doing that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now, if you want to go to the core problem that faces everybody in manufacturing in this country, it’s that agreement that’s about to be put into practice.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: It’s very simple.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Everybody says it’ll create jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Yes, it’ll create bubble jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now, you know, watch this — listen very carefully to this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: One-time surge while we build factories and ship machine tools and equipment down there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Then year after year for decades, they will have jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And I finally — I thought I didn’t understand it — called all the experts, and they said, oh, it’ll be disruptive for 12 to 15 years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We haven’t got 12 days, folks.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We cannot lose those jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: They were eventually saying, Mexican jobs will eventually come to $7.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: 50 an hour, ours will eventually go down to $7.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: 50 an hour.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Makes you feel real good to hear that, right?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Let’s think it through here.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Let’s be careful.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I’m for free trade philosophically, but I have studied these trade agreements till the world has gone flat, and we don’t have good trade agreements across the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I hope we’ll have a chance to get into that tonight, because I can get right to the center of the bull’s-eye and tell you why we’re losing whole industries in this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Oh, no, it will cost jobs, but that’s not — let me say this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I’d rather, if you gave me 2 bad choices —

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I’d rather have some jobs left here than just see everything head south, see?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: No, I’m saying our principal need now is to stabilize the tax base, which is the job base, and create a growing, dynamic base.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now please, folks, if you don’t hear anything else I say, remember where the — millions of people at work are our tax base.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Jim, one quick point.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: If you confiscate the Forbes 400 wealth, take it all, you cannot balance the budget this year.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Kind of gets your head straight about where the taxes, year in and year out, have gotta come from.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Millions and millions of people at work.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m caught in the middle on NAFTA.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Ross says, with great conviction, he opposes the North American Free Trade Agreement.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I am for the North American Free Trade Agreement.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: My problem with Governor Clinton, once again, is that one time he’s gonna make up his mind, he sees some merit in it, but then he sees a lot of things wrong with it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Then the other day he says he’s for it, however then we’ve got to pass other legislation.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: When you’re president of the US, you cannot have this pattern of saying well, I’m for it but I’m on the other side of it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And it’s true on this and it’s true on CAFE.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Look, if Ross were right when we get a free trade agreement with Mexico, why wouldn’t they have gone down there now?

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You have a differential in wages right now.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I just have an honest philosophical difference.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think free trade is going to expand our job opportunity.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think it is exports that have saved us when we’re in a global slowdown, a connected global slowdown, a recession in some countries.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And it’s free trade, fair trade that needs to be our hallmark, and we need more free trade agreements, not fewer.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I’d like to respond to that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: You know, Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Bush was very grateful when I was among the Democrats who said he ought to have the authority to negotiate an agreement with Mexico.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Neither I nor anybody else, as far a I know, agreed to give him our proxy to say that whatever he did was fine for the workers of this country and for the interests of this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I am the one who’s in the middle on this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Perot says it’s a bad deal.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Bush says it’s a hunky-dory deal.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I say on balance it does more good than harm if, if we can get some protection for the environment so that the Mexicans have to follow their own environmental standards, their own labor law standards, and if we have a genuine commitment to reeducate and retrain the American workers who lose their jobs and reinvest in this economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I have a realistic approach to trade.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I want more trade, and I know there are some good things in that agreement.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But it can sure be made better.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Let me just point out, just today in the Los Angeles Times Clyde Prestowitz, who was one of President Reagan’s leading trade advisers and a life-long conservative Republican, endorsed my candidacy because he knows that I’ll have a free and fair trade policy, a hard-headed, realistic policy, and not get caught up in rubber-stamping everything the Bush administration did.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: If I wanted to do that, why would I run for president, Jim?

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Anybody else can run the middle class down and run the economy in a ditch.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I want to change it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think he made my case.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: On the one hand, it’s a good deal but on the other hand I’d make it better.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You can’t do that as president.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You can’t do it on the war, where he says well, I was with the minority but I guess I would have voted with the majority.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: This is my point tonight.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’re talking about 2 weeks from now you’ve gotta decide who’s gonna be president.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And there is this pattern that has plagued him in the primaries and now about trying to have it both ways on all these issues.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You can’t do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And if you make a mistake, say you made a mistake and go on about your business, trying to serve the American people.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Right now we heard it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Ross is against it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I am for it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He says on the one hand I am for it and on the other hand I may be against it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That’s what’s wrong with Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Bush.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: His whole deal is you’ve gotta be for it or against it, you can’t make it better.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I believe we can be better.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think the American people are sick and tired of either/or solutions, people being pushed in the corner, polarized to extremes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: GOVERNOR CLINTON : I want think they want somebody with common sense who can do what’s best for the American people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I’d be happy to discuss these other issues, but I can’t believe he is accusing me of getting on both sides.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: He said trickle-down economics was voodoo economics; now he’s it’s biggest practitioner.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: He promised — he — you know — let me just say —

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But I’ve always said trickle-down government is bad.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I could run this string out a long time, but remember this, Jim.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Those 209 Americans last Thursday night in Richmond told us they wanted us to stop talking about each other and start talking about Americans and their problems and their promise, and I think we ought to get back to that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I’ll be glad to answer any question you have, but this election ought to be about the American people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Is there an equal time rule tonight?

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Yes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Or do you just keep lunging in at will?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I thought we were going to have equal time, but maybe I just have to interrupt the other 2.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Is that the way it works?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now that we’ve talked all around the problem about free trade, let’s go again to the center of the bull’s- eye.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I do, I do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I just want to make — foreign lobbyists, this whole thing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Our country has sold out to foreign lobbyists.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We don’t have free trade.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Both parties have foreign lobbyists on leaves in key roles in their campaigns.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And if there’s anything more unwise than that, I don’t know what it is.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Every debate I bring this up, and nobody ever addresses it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I would like for them to look you in the eye and tell you why they have people representing foreign countries working on their campaigns.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And you know, you’ve seen the list, I’ve seen the list, we won’t go into the names, but no wonder they — if I had those people around me all day every day, telling me it was fair and free, I might believe it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: But if I look at the facts as a businessman, it’s so tilted, the first thing you ought to do is just say, guys, if you like these deals so well, we’ll give you the deal you gave us.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now, Japanese couldn’t unload the cars in this country if they had the same restrictions we had, and on and on and on and on and on.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I suggest to you that the core problem — 1 country spent $400 million lobbying in 1988, our country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And it goes on and on.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And you look at a who’s who in these campaigns around the 2 candidates.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: They’re foreign lobbyists taking leaves.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: What do you think they’re going to do when the campaign’s over?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Go back to work at 30,000 bucks a month representing some other country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I don’t believe that’s in the American people’s interest.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I don’t have a one of them, and I haven’t taken a penny of foreign money, and I never will.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Most people that are lobbying are lobbying the Congress.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I don’t think there’s anything wrong with an honest person who happens to represent an interest of another country for making his case.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s the American way.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And what you’re assuming is that that makes the recipient of the lobbying corrupt or the lobbyist himself corrupt.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t agree with that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But if I found somebody that had a conflict of interest that would try to illegally do something as a foreign — registered lobby, the laws cover this.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t know why — I’ve never understood quite why Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Perot was so upset it, because one of the guys he used to have working for him, I believe, had foreign accounts.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Could be wrong, but I think so.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And as soon as I found it out, he went out the door.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well — But I don’t — I think you got to look at the integrity and the honor of the people that are being lobbied and those that are lobbyists.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The laws protect the American taxpayer in this regard.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: If the laws are violated so much, but to suggest if somebody represents a foreign country on anything, that makes him corrupt or against the taxpayer, I don’t agree with that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: One quick relevant specific.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We’re getting ready to dismantle the airlines industry in our country, and none of you know it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And I doubt in all candor if the president knows it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: But this deal that we’re doing with BAC and US Air and KLM and Northwest, guess who’s on the president’s campaign big time: a guy from Northwest.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: This deal is terribly destructive to the US airline industry.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: One of the largest industries in the world is the travel and tourist business.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We won’t be making airplanes in this country 10 years from now if we let deals like this go through.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: If the president has any interest tonight, I’ll detail it to you; I won’t take 10 minutes tonight.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: All these things take a few minutes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: But that’s happening as we sit here today.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We hammerlock the American companies — American Airlines, Delta — the last few great we have, because we’re trying to do this deal with these 2 European companies.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And never forget, they’ve got Airbus over there, and it’s a government-owned, privately owned, consortium across Europe.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: They’re dying to get the commercial airline business.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Japan is trying to get the commercial airline business.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think there are any villains inside government on this issue, but there’s sure a lot of people who don’t understand business.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And maybe you need somebody up there who understands when you’re getting your pocket picked.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Jim.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Why, I had a great response to that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Just very briefly.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think Ross is right and that we do need some more restrictions on lobbyists.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We ought to make them disclose the people they’ve given money to when they’re testifying before congressional committees; we ought to close the lawyers’ loopholes; they ought to have to disclose when they’re really lobbying.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And we ought to have to limit — we ought to have a much longer period of time, about 5 years, between the time when people can leave executive branch offices and then go out and start lobbying for foreign interests.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I agree with that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We’ve wrecked the airline industry already because of all these leverage buyouts and all these terrible things that have happened to the airline industry.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We’re going to have a hard time rebuilding it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But the real thing we got to have is a competitive economic strategy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Look what’s happening to McDonnell Douglas; even Boeing is losing market share — because we let the Europeans spend $25-$40 billion on Airbus without an appropriate competitive response.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: What I want America to do is to trade more but to compete and win by investing in competitive ways.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And we’re in real trouble on that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I promise it’s less than 10 seconds.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I heard Gov Clinton congratulate us on 1 thing — first time he said something pleasant about this administration.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Productivity in this country is up, it is way up — productivity is up.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And that’s a good thing.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: There are many good ones, but I was glad he acknowledged that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Thank you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now give me 1 second…

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I’ve volunteered.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now, look, I’m just kind of a, you know, cur dog here; I was put on the ballot by the people, not special interests.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: So I have to stand up for myself.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now, Jim, let me get it out.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: On the 2nd debate, I offered, since both sides want the enterprise zones and we can’t get together, I said I’ll take a few days off and go to Washington and hold hands with you and we’ll get it done.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I’ll take a few days off and hold hands with you and get this airlines thing straightened, because that’s important to this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: That’s kind of pathetic I have to do it — and nobody’s called me yet to come up, I might mention.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: But if they do — if they do, it’s easy to fix.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: If you all want the enterprise zones, why don’t we pass the dang thing and do it, right?

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Uh-uh.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Uh-uh.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: If I had it to do over again I might answer the questions a little better.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: You know, I’d been in public life a long time and no one had ever questioned my role and so I was asked a lot of questions about things that happened a long time ago and I don’t think I answered them as well as I could have.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Going back 23 years, I don’t know, Helen.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I was opposed to the war.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I couldn’t help that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I felt very strongly about it, and I didn’t want to go at the time.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It’s easy to say in retrospect I would have done something differently.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: President Lincoln opposed the war and there were people who said maybe he shouldn’t be president, but I think he made us a pretty good president in wartime.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We’ve had a lot of other presidents who didn’t wear their country’s uniform who had to order our young soldiers into battle, including President Wilson and President Roosevelt.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So the answer is I could do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I wouldn’t relish doing it but I wouldn’t shrink from it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think that the president has to be prepared to use the power of the nation when our vital interests are threatened, when our treaty commitments are at stake, when we know that something has to be done that is in the national interest, and that is a part of being president.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Could I do it?

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Yes, I could.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, I’ve expressed my heartfelt difference with Governor Clinton on organizing demonstrations while in a foreign land against your country, when young ghetto kids have been drafted and are dying.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: My argument with him on — the question was about the draft — is that there’s this same pattern.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: In New Hampshire Senator Kerrey said you ought to level, you ought to tell the truth about it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: On April 17 he said he’d bring out all the records on the draft.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: They have not been forthcoming.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He got a deferment or he didn’t.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He got a notice or he didn’t.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I think it’s this pattern that troubles me, more than the draft.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: A lot of decent, honorable people felt as he did on the draft.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But it’s this pattern.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And again, you might be able to make amendments all the time, Governor, but you’ve got to, as president, you can’t be on all these different sides, and you can’t have this pattern of saying well, I did this or I didn’t, then the facts come out and you change it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s my big difference with him on the draft.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It wasn’t failing to serve.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Yes, sir.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Helen?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I’ve spent my whole adult life very close to the military.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I feel very strongly about the people who go into battle for our country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I appreciate their idealism, their sacrifices.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Appreciate the sacrifices their families make.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: That’s been displayed again and again in a very tangible way.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I look on this as history.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I don’t look on it personally as relevant, and I consider it really a waste of time tonight, when you consider the issues that face our country right now.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I wouldn’t have taken any of the alternatives.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I believe that — I believe I made a mistake.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I did it for the very reasons you say.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: There was one good thing that came out of that budget agreement, and that is we put a cap on discretionary spending.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: One-third of the president’s budget is at the president’s discretion, or really the Congress, since they appropriate every dime and tell a president how to spend every dime.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’ve put a cap on the growth of all that spending, and that’s good and that’s helped.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But I was wrong because I thought the tax compromise, going along with 1 Democratic tax increase, would help the economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I see no evidence that it has done it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So what would I have done?

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: What should I have done?

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I should have held out for a better deal that would have protected the taxpayer and not ended up doing what we had to do, or what I thought at the time would help.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So I made a mistake, and I — you know, the difference, I think, is that I knew at the time I was going to take a lot of political flak.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I knew we’d have somebody out there yelling “read my lips”, and I did it because I thought it was right.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I made a mistake.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s quite different than taking a position where you know it’s best for you.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That wasn’t best for me and I knew it in the very beginning.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I thought it would be better for the country than it was.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So there we are.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: 101 in leadership is be accountable for what you do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Let’s go back to the tax and budget summit briefly.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Nobody ever told the American people that we increased spending $1.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: 83 for every dollar of taxes raised.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: That’s absolutely unconscionable.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Both parties carry a huge blame for that on their shoulders.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: This was not a way to pay down the deficit.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: This was a trick on the American people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: That’s not leadership.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Let’s go back in terms of accepting responsibility for your actions.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: If you create Saddam Hussein, over a 10-year period, using billions of dollars of US taxpayer money, step up to the plate and say it was a mistake.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: If you create Noriega, using taxpayer money, step up to the plate and say it was a mistake.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: If you can’t get your act together to pick him up one day when a Panamanian major has kidnapped him and a special forces team is 400 yards away and it’s a stroll across the park to get him, and if you can’t get your act together, at least pick up the Panamanian major, who they then killed, step up to the plate and admit it was a mistake.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: That’s leadership, folks.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now, leaders will always make mistakes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We’ve created, and I’m not aiming at any one person here, I’m aiming at our government — nobody takes responsibility for anything.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We’ve gotta change that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I’m watching the lights.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The mistake that was made was making the “read my lips” promise in the first place just to get elected, knowing what the size of the deficit was.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Knowing what the size of the deficit was, knowing there was no plan to control health care costs and knowing that we did not have a strategy to get real economic growth back into this economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The choices were not good then.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think at the time, the mistake that was made was signing off on the deal late on Saturday night in the middle of the night.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That’s just what the president did when he vetoed the Family Leave Act.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think what he should have done is gone before the American people on the front end and said listen, I made a commitment and it was wrong.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I made a mistake because I couldn’t have foreseen these circumstances and this is the best deal we can work out at the time.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: He said it was in the public interest at the time and most everybody who was involved in it, I guess, thought it was.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The real mistake was the “read my lips” promise in the first place.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: You just can’t promise something like that just to get elected if you know there’s a good chance that circumstances may overtake you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: You’re talking about 2 different subjects.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: In order to lead, you first have to use the White House as a bully pulpit and lead; then you have to develop consensus or you can’t get anything done, and that’s where we are now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We can’t get anything done.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: How do you get anything done when you’ve got all of these political action committees, all of these thousands of registered lobbyists — 40,000 registered lobbyists, 23,000 special interest groups — and the list goes on and on and on.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And the average citizen out here is just working hard every day.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: You’ve got to go to the people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I just love the fact that everybody, particularly in the media, goes bonkers over the town hall.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I guess it’s because you will lose your right to tell them what to think.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: The point is, they’ll get to decide what to think.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I love the fact that people will listen to a guy with a bad accent and a poor presentation manner talking about flip charts for 30 minutes, because they want the details.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: See, all the folks up there at the top said the attention span of the American people is no more than 5 minutes, they won’t watch it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: They’re thirsty for it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: You want to have a new program in this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: If you get grassroots America excited about it, and if they tap Congress on the shoulder and say do it, Charlie, it’ll happen.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
