transcript_turns.text: And that’s a whole lot different from these fellows running up and down the halls whispering in their ears now and promising campaign funds for the next election if they do it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now, I think that’s going back to where we started.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: That’s having a government from the people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I think that’s the essence of leadership, rather than cutting deals in dark rooms in Washington.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Well, I believe in the town hall meetings; they started with my campaign in New Hampshire.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I think Ross Perot has done a good job in having them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I, as you know, pushed for the debate to include the 209 American citizens who were part of it in Richmond a few days ago.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I’ve done a lot of them, and I’ll continue to do them as president.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But I’d also like to point out that I haven’t been part of what we’re criticizing in Washington tonight.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Of the 3 of us, I have balanced a government budget 12 times, I have offered and passed campaign finance reform, offered, pushed for and passed in public referendum lobbyist restrictions, done the kinds of things you have to do to get legislators together not only to establish consensus but to challenge them to change.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And in 12 years as governor I guess I’ve taken on every interest group there was in my state at one time or another to fight for change.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It can be done.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That’s why I tried to be so specific in this campaign to have a mandate, if elected, so that Congress will know what the American people have voted for.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I would like the record to show the panelists that Ross Perot took the first shot at the press.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: My favorite bumper sticker, though, is: Annoy the Media.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Re-elect President Bush.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I just had to work that in.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Sorry, Helen.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m going to pay for this later on.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Look, you have to build a consensus, but in some things — Ross mentioned Saddam Hussein.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Yes, we tried, and, yes, we failed to bring him into the family of nations; he had the 4th largest army.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But then when he moved against Kuwait, I said this will not stand.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And it’s hard to build a consensus.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We went to the UN, we made historic resolutions up there, the whole world was united, our Congress was dragging its feet.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Governor Clinton said, well, I might have been with the minority, let sanctions work — but I guess I would have voted with the majority.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: A president can’t do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Sometimes he has to act.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And in this case I’m glad we did, because if we had let sanctions work and tried to build a consensus on that, Saddam Hussein today would be in Saudi Arabia controlling the world’s oil supply, and he would be there maybe with a nuclear weapon.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We busted the 4th largest army, and we did it through leadership.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You don’t see Margaret Tutwiler sitting in there with me today.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Huh?

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I happen to think she’s a key person.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think our Cabinet members are key people.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think the woman that works with me, Rose Zamaria, is about as tough as a boot out there and makes some discipline and protects the taxpayer.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Look at our Cabinet.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You talk about somebody strong.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Look at Carla Hills.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Look at Lynn Martin, who’s fighting against this glass ceiling and doing a first-class job on it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Look at our surgeon general, Dr.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Novello.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You can look all around and you’ll see first-class strong women.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Jim Baker’s a man.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Yeah, I plead guilty to that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But look who’s around with him there.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I mean, this is a little defensive on your part, Susan, to be honest with you.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got a very good record appointing women to high positions and positions of trust, and I’m not defensive at all about it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: What we got to do is keep working, as the Labor Dept is doing a first-class job on, to break down discrimination, to break down the glass ceiling.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I am not apologetic at all about our record with women.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got, I think — you know, you think about women in government, I think about women in business.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Why not try to help them with my small business program to build some incentives into the system?

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think we’re making progress here.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You got a lot of women running for office.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: As I said the other night, I hope a lot of them lose because they’re liberal Democrats — — and we don’t need more of them in the Senate or more of them in the House.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But nevertheless, they’re out there.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And we got some very good Republican women running.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So we’re making dramatic progress.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Well, I come from the computer business, and everybody knows the women are more talented than the men.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: So we have a long history of having a lot of talented women.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: One of our first officers was a woman, the chief financial officer.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: She was a director.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And it was so far back, it was considered so odd, and even though we were a tiny, little company at the time, it made all the national magazines.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: But in terms of being influenced by women and being a minority, there they are right out there, my wife and my 4 beautiful daughters, and I just have 1 son, so he and I are surrounded by women, giving — telling us what to do all the time.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And the rest of my minute, I want to make a very brief comment here in terms of Saddam Hussein.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We told him that we wouldn’t get involved with his border dispute, and we’ve never revealed those papers that were given to Ambassador Glaspie on July the 25th.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I suggest, in the sense of taking responsibility for your actions, we lay those papers on the table.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: They’re not the secrets to the nuclear bomb.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Secondly, we got upset when he took the whole thing, but to the ordinary American out there who doesn’t know where the oil fields are in Kuwait, they’re near the border.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We told him he could take the northern part of Kuwait, and when he took the whole thing, we went nuts.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And if we didn’t tell him that, why won’t we even let the Senate Foreign Relations Committee and the Senate Intelligence Committee see the written instructions for Ambassador Glaspie?

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’ve got reply on that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That gets to the national honor.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We did not say to Saddam Hussein, Ross, you can take the northern part of Kuwait.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Well, where are the papers?

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That is absolutely absurd.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Where are the papers?

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Glaspie has testified — — and Glaspie’s papers have been presented to the US Senate.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Please, let’s be factual.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: If you have time, go through Nexis and Lexis, pull all the old news articles, look at what Ambassador Glaspie said all through the fall and what-have-you, and then look at what she and Kelly and all the others in State said at the end when they were trying to clean it up.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And talk to any head of any of those key committees in the Senate.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: They will not let them see the written instructions given to Ambassador Glaspie.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And I suggest that in a free society owned by the people, the American people ought to know what we told Ambassador Glaspie to tell Saddam Hussein, because we spent a lot of money and risked lives and lost lives in that effort, and did not accomplish most of our objectives.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We got Kuwait back to the emir but he’s still not his nuclear, his chemical, his bacteriological and he’s still over there, right?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I’d like to see those written instructions.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: For which I apologize.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: When I make a mistake I say I’m sorry.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: No, I don’t.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I apologize for it but that one got right to the national honor and I’m sorry.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I just couldn’t let it stand.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Susan, I don’t agree that there are no women and minorities in important positions in my campaign.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: There are many.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But I think even more relevant is my record at home.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: For most of my time as governor a woman was my chief of staff.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: An African American was my chief cabinet officer.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: An African American was my chief economic development officer.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It was interesting today.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: There was a story today or yesterday in the Washington Post about my economic programs and my chief budget officer and my chief economic officer were both African Americans, even though the Post didn’t mention that, which I think is a sign of progress.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The Natl Women’s Political Caucus gave me an award, one of their Good Guy Awards, for my involvement of women in high levels of government, and I’ve appointed more minorities to positions of high level in government than all the governors in the history of my state combined, before me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So that’s what I’ll do as president.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think we’ve got a person to waste and I think I owe the American people a White House staff, a Cabinet and appointments that look like America but that meet high standards of excellence, and that’s what I’ll do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: No.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: They’re not correct and if you look at my life, until I got involved in this effort, I was one person.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And then after the Republican dirty tricks group got through with me I’m another person, which I consider an absolutely sick operation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And all of you in the press know exactly what I’m talking about.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: They investigated every single one of my children.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: They investigated my wife.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: They interviewed all of my children’s friends from childhood on.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: They went to extraordinary sick lengths, and I just found it amusing that they would take 2 or 3 cases where I was involved in lawsuits and would engage an investigator — the lawyers would engage an investigator, which is common.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And the only difference between me and any other businessman that has the range of businesses that I have is I haven’t had that many lawsuits.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: So that’s just another one of those little fruit-loopy things they make up to try to, instead of facing issues, to try to redefine a person that’s running against them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: This goes on night and day.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I will do everything I can, if I get up there, to make dirty tricks a thing of the past.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: One of the 2 groups has raised it to an art form.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: It’s a sick art form.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now, let’s go back to Saddam Hussein.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We gave Ambassador Glaspie written instructions.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: That’s a fact.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We’ve never let the Congress and the Foreign Relations, Senate Intelligence Committees see them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: That’s a fact.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Ambassador Glaspie did a lot of talking right after July 25 and that’s a fact and it’s in all the newspapers.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And you pull all of it at once and read it and I did, and it’s pretty clear what she and Kelly and the other key guys around that thing thought they were doing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Then at the end of the war, when they had to go testify about it, their stories are a total disconnect from what they said in August, September and October.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: So I say this is very simple.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Saddam Hussein released a tape, as you know, claiming it was a transcript of their meeting, where she said we will not become involved in your border dispute and, in effect, you can take the northern part of the country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We later said no, that’s not true.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I said well, this is simple.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: What were her written instructions?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We guard those like the secrets of the atomic bomb, literally.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now, I say whose country is this?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: This is ours.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Who will get hurt if we lay those papers on the table?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: The worst thing is, again, it’s a mistake.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Nobody did any of this with evil intent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I just object to the fact that we cover up and hide things.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Whether it’s Iran-contra, Iraq-gate or you name it, it’s a steady stream.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Let’s take Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Bush for the moment at his word — he’s right, we don’t have any evidence at least that our government did tell Saddam Hussein he could have that part of Kuwait.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And let’s give him the credit he deserves for organizing Operation Desert Storm and Desert Shield.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It was a remarkable event.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But let’s look at where I think the real mistake was made.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: In 1988 when the war between Iraq and Iran ended, we knew Saddam Hussein was a tyrant, we had dealt with him because he was against Iran — the enemy of my enemy maybe is my friend.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: All right, the war’s over; we know he’s dropping mustard gas on his own people, we know he’s threatened to incinerate half of Israel.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Several government departments — several — had information that he was converting our aid to military purposes and trying to develop weapons of mass destruction.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But in late ’89 the president signed a secret policy saying we were going to continue to try to improve relations with him, and we sent him some sort of communication on the eve of his invasion of Kuwait that we still wanted better relations.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So I think what was wrong — I give credit where credit is due — but the responsibility was in coddling Saddam Hussein when there was no reason to do it and when people at high levels in our government knew he was trying to do things that were outrageous.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, it’s awful easy when you’re dealing with 90-90 hindsight.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We did try to bring Saddam Hussein into the family of nations; he did have the 4th largest army.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: All our Arab allies out there thought we ought to do just exactly that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And when he crossed the line, I stood up and looked into the camera and I said: This aggression will not stand.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And we formed a historic coalition, and we brought him down, and we destroyed the 4th largest army.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And the battlefield was searched, and there wasn’t one single iota of evidence that any US weapons were on that battlefield.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And the nuclear capability has been searched by the United Nations, and there hasn’t been one single scintilla of evidence that there’s any US technology involved in it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And what you’re seeing on all this Iraq-gate is a bunch of people who were wrong on the war trying to cover their necks here and try to do a little revisionism.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I cannot let that stand, because it isn’t true.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Yes, we had grain credits for Iraq, and there isn’t any evidence that those grain credits were diverted into weaponry — none, none whatsoever.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And so I just have to say, it’s fine.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You can’t stand there, Governor Clinton, and say, well, I think I’d have been — I have supported the minority, let sanctions work or wish it would go away — but I would have voted with the majority.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Come on, that’s not leadership.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Gene, there is a problem in the sense that there are some problem banks, and on December 19th new regulations will go into effect which will in effect give the government the responsibility to close some banks that are not technically insolvent but that are plainly in trouble.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: On the other hand, I don’t think that we have any reason to believe that the dimensions of this crisis are anywhere near as great as the savings and loan crisis.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The mistake that both parties made in Washington with the S&L business was deregulating them without proper capital requirements, proper oversight and regulation, proper training of the executives.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Many people predicted what happened, and it was a disaster.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The banking system in this country is fundamentally sound with some weak banks.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think that our goal ought to be first of all not to politicize it, not to frighten people; secondly to say that we have to enforce the law in 2 ways.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We don’t want to overreact, as the federal regulators have in my judgment, on good banks so that they’ve created credit crunches, that is, they have made our recession worse in the last couple of years — but we do want to act prudently with the banks that are in trouble.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We also want to say that insofar as is humanly possible the banking industry itself should pay for the cost of any bank failures; the taxpayers should not.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And that will be my policy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I believe if we have a good balanced approach, we can get the good banks loaning money again, end the credit crunch, have proper regulation on the ones that are in trouble, and not overreact.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It is a serious problem, but I don’t see it as the kind of terrible, terrible problem that the S&L problem was.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, I don’t believe it would be appropriate for a president to suggest that the banking system is not sound.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It is sound.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: There are some problem banks out there.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But what we need is financial reform; we need some real financial reform, banking reform legislation.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I have proposed that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And when I am re-elected, I believe one of the first things ought to be to press a new Congress not beholden to the old ways to pass financial reform legislation that modernizes the banking system, doesn’t put a lot of inhibitions on it, and protects the depositors through keeping the FDIC sound.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But I think that — I just was watching some of the proceedings of the American Bankers Assn, and I think the general feeling is most of the banks are sound, certainly there’s no comparison here between what happened to the S&Ls and where the banks stand right now, in my view.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Well, nobody’s gotten into the real issue yet on the savings and loan again — nobody’s got a business background, I guess.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: The whole problem came up in 1984.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: The president of the US was told officially it was a $20-billion problem.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: These crooks — now, Willie Sutton would have gone to own a savings and loan rather than rob banks, because he robbed banks because that’s where the money is; owning a savings and loan is where the money was.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now, in 1984 they were told.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I believe the vice president was in charge of deregulation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Nobody touched that tar baby till the day after election in 1988 because they were flooding both parties with crooked PAC money, and it was in many cases stolen PAC money.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now, you and I never got a ride on a lot of these yachts and fancy things it bought, but you and I are paying for it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And they buried it till right after the election.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now, if you believe The Washington Post and you believe this extensive study that’s been done — and I’m reading it — right after election day this year they’re going to hit us with a hundred banks, it will be a $100-billion problem.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now, if that’s true, just tell me now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I’m grownup, I can deal with it, I’ll pay my share.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: But just tell me now; don’t bury until after the election twice.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I say that to both political parties.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: The people deserve that since we have to pick up the tab; you got the PAC money, we’ll pay the tab.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Just tell us.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: The debt and the deficit.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Well, if you watched my television show the other night, you saw it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And if you watch it Thursday, Friday, Saturday this week, you’ll get more.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: A shameless plug there, Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: President.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: But in a nutshell we’ve got to reform our government or we won’t get anything done.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We have a government that doesn’t work.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: All these specific examples I’m giving tonight — if you had a business like that, they’d be leading you away and boarding up the doors.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We have a government that doesn’t work.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: It’s supposed to come from the people, it comes at the people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: The people need to take their government back.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: You’ve got to reform Congress, they’ve got to be servants of the people again; you’ve got to reform the White House.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to turn this thing around.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And it’s a long list of specific items.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And I’ve covered it again and again in print and on television.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: But very specifically the key thing is to turn the government back to the people and take it away from the special interests and have people go to Washington to serve.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Who can give themselves a 23% pay raise anywhere in the world except Congress?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Who would have 1200 airplanes worth 2 billion a year just to fly around in?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I don’t have a free reserved parking place at Natl Airport, why should my servants?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I don’t have an indoor gymnasium and an indoor tennis and an indoor every other thing they can think of; I don’t have a place where I can go make free TV to send to my constituents to try to brainwash them to elect me the next time.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And I’m paying for all that for those guys.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I’m going to be running an ad pretty soon that shows they promised us they were going to hold the line on spending at the tax and budget summit, and I’m going to show how much they’ve increased this little stuff they do for themselves.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And it is silly putty, folks, and the American people have had enough of it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Step one, if I get up there, we’re going to clean that up.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: You say, how can I get Congress to do that?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I’ll have millions of people at my shoulder, shoulder to shoulder with me, and we will see it done work speed — because it’s wrong.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We’ve turned the country upside down.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I would just point out, on the point Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Perot made, I agree that we need to cut spending in Congress.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I’ve called for a 25% reduction in congressional staffs and expenditures.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But the White House staff increased its expenditures by considerably more than Congress has in the last 4 years under the Bush administration, and Congress has actually spent a billion dollars less than President Bush asked them to spend.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Now, when you out-spend Congress you’re really swinging.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That, however, is not my only passion.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The real problem in this country is that most people are working hard and falling farther behind.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: My passion is to pass a jobs program and get incomes up with an investment incentive program to grow jobs in the private sector, to waste less public money and invest more, to control health care costs and provide for affordable health care for all Americans and to make sure we’ve got the best trained workforce in the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That is my passion.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We’ve gotta get this country growing again and this economy strong again or we can’t bring down the deficit.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Economic growth is the key to the future of this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: On government reform?

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Government reform?

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, how about this for a government reform policy?

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Reduce the White House staff by a 3rd after or at the same time the Congress does the same thing for their staff.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Term limits for members of the US Congress.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Give the government back to the people.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Let’s do it that way.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The president has term limits.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Let’s limit some of these guys sitting out here tonight.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Term limits.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And then how about a balanced budget amendment to the Constitution?

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Forty-3 — more than that — states have it, I believe.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Let’s try that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And you want to do something about all this extra spending that concerns Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Perot and me?

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Okay.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: How about a line item veto?

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Forty-three governors have that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And give it to the president, and if the Congress isn’t big enough to do it, let the president have a shot at this excess spending.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: A line item veto.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That means you can take a line and cut out some of the pork out of a meaningful bill.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Governor Clinton keeps hitting me on vetoing legislation.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, that’s the only protection the taxpayer has against some of these reckless pork programs up there, and I’d rather be able to just line it right out of there and get on about passing some good stuff but leave out the garbage.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Line item veto — there’s a good reform program for you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: My plan — you can read my plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: My plan says that we want to raise marginal incomes on family incomes above $200,000 from 31 to 36 percent, that we want to ask foreign corporations simply to pay the same percentage of taxes on their income that American corporations play in America, that we want to use that money to provide over $100 billion in tax cuts for investment in new plant and equipment, for small business, for new technologies, and for middle class tax relief.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Now, I’ll tell ya this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I will not raise taxes on the middle class to pay for these programs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: If the money does not come in there to pay for these programs, we will cut other government spending or we will slow down the phase-in of the programs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I am not gonna raise taxes on the middle class to pay for these programs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Now furthermore, I am not gonna tell you “read my lips” on anything because I cannot foresee what emergencies might develop in this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And the president said never, never, never would he raise taxes in New Jersey, and within a day Marlin Fitzwater, his spokesman, said now, that’s not a promise.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So I think even he has learned that you can’t say “read my lips” because you can’t know what emergencies might come up.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But I can tell you this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I’m not gonna raise taxes on middle class Americans to pay for the programs I’ve recommended.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Read my plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And you know how you can trust me about that?

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Because you know, in the first debate, Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Bush made some news.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: He’d just said Jim Baker was going to be secretary of state and in the first debate he said no, now he’s gonna be responsible for domestic economic policy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Well, I’ll tell ya.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I’ll make some news in the 3rd debate.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The person responsible for domestic economic policy in my administration will be Bill Clinton.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I’m gonna make those decisions, and I won’t raise taxes on the middle class to pay for my programs.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s what worries me — — that he’s going to be responsible.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He’s going to do — and he would do for the US what he’s done to Arkansas.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He would do for the US what he’s done to Arkansas.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We do not want to be the lowest of the low.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We are not a nation in decline.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We are a rising nation.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Now, my problem is — I heard what he said.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He said I want to take it from the rich, raise $150 billion from the rich.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: To get it, to get $150 billion in new taxes, you got to go down to the guy that’s making $36,600.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And if you want to pay for the rest of his plan, all the other spending programs, you’re going to sock it to the working man.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So when you hear “tax the rich,” Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: and Mrs.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: America, watch your wallet.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Lock your wallet because he’s coming right after you just like Jimmy Carter did and just like you’re going to get — you’re going to end up with interest rates at 21%, and you’re going to have inflation going through the roof.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Yes, we’re having tough times, but we do not need to go back to the failed policies of the past, when you had a Democratic president and a spendthrift Democratic Congress.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Jim, you permitted Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Bush to break the rules, he said, to defend the honor of the country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: What about the honor of my state?

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We rank first in the country in job growth, we got the lowest spending, state and local, in the country, and the 2nd lowest tax burden.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And the difference between Arkansas and the US is that we’re going in the right direction and this country’s going in the wrong direction.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I have to defend the honor of my state.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: So I’m the only one that’s untarnished at this point?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I’m sure I’ll do it before it’s over.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Key thing here, see, we all come up with images.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Images don’t fix anything.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I think — you know, I’m starting to understand it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: You stay around this long enough, you think about — if you talk about it in Washington, you think you did it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: If you’ve been on television about it, you think you did it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: What we need is people to stop talking and start doing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now, our real problem here is they both have plans that will not work.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: The Wall Street Journal said your numbers don’t add up.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And you can take it out on charts, you look at all the studies the different groups have done, you go out 4, 5, 6 years, we’re still drifting along with a huge deficit.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: So let’s come back to harsh reality, and what I — you know, everybody says, gee, Perot, you’re tough.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I’m saying, well, this is not as tough as World War II and it’s not as tough as the revolution.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And it’s fair, shared sacrifice to do the right thing for our country and for our children.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And it will be fun if we all work together to do it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, I think the answer to why the drop, I think, has been the economy in the doldrums.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Why I’ll win is I think I have the best plan of the 3 of us up here to do something about it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Mine does not grow the government, it does not invest, have government invest.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It says we need to do better in terms of stimulating private business.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We got a big philosophical difference here tonight between one who thinks the government can do all these things through tax and spend, and one who thinks it ought to go the other way.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And so I believe the answer is, I’m going to win it because I’m getting into focus my agenda for America’s renewal, and also I think that Governor Clinton’s had pretty much of a free ride.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: On looking specifically at the Arkansas record — he keeps criticizing us, criticizing me, I’m the incumbent, fine.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But he’s an incumbent, and we’ve got to look at all the facts.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: They’re almost at the bottom on every single category.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We can’t do that to the American people.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And then, Helen, I really believe where people are going to ask this question about trust, because I do think there’s a pattern by Governor Clinton of saying one thing to please one group, and then trying to please another group.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I think that pattern is a dangerous thing to suggest would work for the Oval Office.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It doesn’t work that way when you’re president.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Truman is right.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The buck stops there.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And you have to make decisions even when it’s against your own interest.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I’ve done that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s against my political interest to say go ahead and go along with the tax increase, but I did what I thought was right at the time.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So I think people are going to be looking for trust and experience.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And then, I mentioned it the other night, I think if there’s a crisis, people are going to say, well, George Bush has taken us through some tough crises, and we trust him to do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And so I’ll make the appeal on a wide array of issues.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Also I got a philosophical difference.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I got to watch the clock here.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think we’re a declining nation.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The whole world has had economic problems.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’re doing better than a lot of the countries in the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And we’re going to lead the way out of this economic recession across this world and economic slowdown here at home.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s why I think I’ll win.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I’m the last one, right?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: One minute after you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I’m totally focussed on the fact that we may have bank failures and nobody answered it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I’m totally focussed on the fact that we are still evading the issue of the Glaspie papers.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I’m totally focussed on the fact that we still could have enterprise zones, according to both parties, but we don’t.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: So I am still focussed on gridlock, I guess.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And I am also focussed on the fact that isn’t it a paradox that we have the highest productivity in our workforce in the industrialized world and at the same time have the largest trade deficit, and at the same time rank behind 9 other nations in what we pay our most productive people in the world, and we’re losing whole industries overseas.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now, can’t somebody agree with me that the government is breaking business’s legs with these trade agreements?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: They’re breaking business’s legs in a number of different ways.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We have an adversarial relationship that’s destroying jobs and sending them overseas while we have the finest workers in the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Keep in mind a factory worker has nothing to do with anything except putting it together on the factory floor.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: It’s our obligation to make sure that we give him the finest products in the world to put together and we don’t break his legs in the process.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I really can’t believe Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Bush is still trying to make trust an issue after “read my lips” and 15 million new jobs and embracing what he called voodoo economics and embracing an export enhancement program for farmers he threatened to veto and going all around the country giving out money in programs that he once opposed.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But the main thing is he still didn’t get it, from what he said the other night to that fine woman on our program, the 209 people in Richmond.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: They don’t want us talking about each other.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: They want us to talk about the problems of this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think he’ll be reelected because trickle down economics is a failure and he’s offering more of it, and what he’s saying about my program is just not true.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Look at the Republicans that have endorsed me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: High tech executives in Northern California.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Look at the 24 generals and admirals, retired, that have endorsed me, including the deputy commander of Desert Storm.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Look at Sarah Brady, Jim Brady’s wife, President Reagan’s press secretary, who endorsed me because he knuckled under to the NRA and wouldn’t fight for the Brady Bill.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got a broad-based coalition that goes beyond party because I am going to change this country and make it better, with the help of the American people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: First, I’d like to thank the commission and my opponents for participating in these debates and making them possible.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think the real winners of the debates were the American people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I was especially moved in Richmond a few days ago when 209 of our fellow citizens got to ask us questions.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: They went a long way toward reclaiming this election for the American people and taking their country back.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I want to say, since this is the last time I’ll be on a platform with my opponents, that even though I disagree with Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Perot on how fast we can reduce the deficit and how much we can increase taxes on the middle class, I really respect what he’s done in this campaign to bring the issue of deficit reduction to our attention.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I’d like to say to Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Bush, even though I’ve got profound differences with him, I do honor his service to our country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I appreciate his efforts and I wish him well.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I just believe it’s time to change.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I offer a new approach.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It’s not trickle down economics.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It’s been tried for 12 years and it’s failed.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: More people are working harder for less, 100,000 people a month losing their health insurance, unemployment going up, our economy slowing down.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We can do better.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And it’s not tax and spend economics.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It’s invest and grow, put our people first, control health care costs and provide basic health care to all Americans, have an education system 2nd to none and revitalize the private economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That is my commitment to you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It is the kind of change that can open up a whole new world of opportunities to America as we enter the last decade of this century and move towards the 21st century.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I want a country where people who work hard and play by the rules are rewarded, not punished.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I want a country where people are coming together across the lines of race and region and income.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I know we can do better.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It won’t take miracles and it won’t happen overnight, but we can do much, much better if we have the courage to change.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Thank you very much.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Three weeks from now — 2 weeks from tomorrow, America goes to the polls and you’re going to have to decide who you want to lead this country to economic recovery.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: On jobs — that’s the number one priority, and I believe my program for stimulating investment, encouraging small business, brand-new approach to education, strengthening the American family, and, yes, creating more exports is the way to go.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t believe in trickle-down government, I don’t believe in larger taxes and larger government spending.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: On foreign affairs, some think it’s irrelevant.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I believe it’s not.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’re living in an interconnected world.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The whole world is having economic difficulties.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The US is doing better than a lot.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But we’ve got to do even better.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And if a crisis comes up, I ask who has the judgment and the experience and, yes, the character to make the right decision?

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And, lastly, the other night on character Governor Clinton said it’s not the character of the president but the character of the presidency.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I couldn’t disagree more.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Horace Greeley said the only thing that endures is character.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I think it was Justice Black who talked about great nations, like great men, must keep their word.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And so the question is, who will safeguard this nation, who will safeguard our people and our children?

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I need your support, I ask for your vote.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And may God bless the US of America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: To the millions of fine decent people who did the unthinkable and took their country back in their own hands and put me on the ballot, let me pledge to you that tonight is just the beginning.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: These next 2 weeks we will be going full steam ahead to make sure that you get a voice and that you get your country back.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: This Thursday night on ABC from 8:30 to 9, Friday night on NBC from 8 to 8:30, and Saturday night on CBS from 8 to 8:30, we’ll be down in the trenches under the hood working on fixin’ the old car to get it back on the road.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now, the question is, can we win?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Absolutely we can win, because it’s your country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Question really is who do you want in the White House.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: It’s that simple.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now, you got to stop letting these people tell you who to vote for, you got to stop letting these folks in the press tell you you’re throwing your vote away — you got to start using your own head.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Then the question is, can we govern?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I love that one.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: The “we” is you and me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: You bet your hat we can govern because we will be in there together and we will figure out what to do, and you won’t tolerate gridlock, you won’t tolerate endless meandering and wandering around, and you won’t tolerate non-performance.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And, believe me, anybody that knows me understands I have a very low tolerance for non-performance also.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Together we can get anything done.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: The president mentioned that you need the right person in a crisis.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Well, folks, we got one, and that one is a financial crisis.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Pretty simply, who’s the best-qualified person up here on the stage to create jobs?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Make your decision and vote on November the 3rd.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I suggest you might consider somebody who’s created jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Who’s the best person to manage money?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I suggest you pick a person who’s successfully managed money.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Who’s the best person to get results and not talk?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Look at the record and make your decision.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And, finally, who would you give your pension fund and your savings account to manage?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And, last one, who would you ask to be the trustee of your estate and take care of your children if something happened to you?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Finally, to you students up there — God bless you, I’m doing this for you: I want you to have the American dream.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: To the American people, I’m doing this because I love you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: That’s it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Thank you very much.
